observations: Stacks of used car tires on dirt ground in an outdoor tire market.
Many tires have orange spray-painted marks such as 'YES' and 'NO'.
Treads look worn and sidewalls are dirty; no brand or country-of-origin text is legible.
Background shows alloy wheels displayed on a shop wall.
A 'POSTED ON JIJI IKWE ANTHONY' watermark appears across the images.

claims.evidence: Photos show used tires but no sidewall branding, DOT code, or 'Made in Belgium' marking is visible.

risks.risk: Remaining tread depth and safe usable life
risks.proof: Close-up photo of tread with a depth gauge or coin for scale

risks.risk: Tire age and rubber perishing (DOT date code)
risks.proof: Sidewall photo showing the DOT code
risks.if_unproven: as old rubber with unknown service life

risks.risk: Hidden punctures, patches, or internal damage
risks.proof: Video of tires inflated and checked for leaks

risks.risk: Claimed Belgian origin cannot be confirmed
risks.proof: Clear sidewall photo showing brand and country of manufacture
risks.if_unproven: as generic used tires, not Belgian

proof_requests: Sidewall close-up showing brand, size, DOT code, and country of origin
Tread close-up on several tires to gauge remaining life
Video showing tires holding air with no visible punctures
response.reason: The photos clearly show used car tires, so the item can be priced at its worst case as unproven part-worn tires; the Belgium and first-grade claims need proof to raise value.
